Zuko Nonxuba wheelchair handover

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Armand Du Plessis, MR SA 2016 and an advocate has managed to get a company to sponsor two wheelchairs for both children from this story

IDEA: Diary cam journey from JHB to the rural EC to give these kids and their families a small ray of light


Further information:
I gave all the footage to Bryan, so he has it.

I don't know how these things work, but If its 5 minutes I can do it with an editor for two days as a commissioned story and manage the whole thing, but just let me know.

Script:



VO1: A few weeks ago, we brought you the horrific story of rogue litigation lawyer, Zuko Nonxuba who had allegedly been stealing Millions in medical negligence claims from clients since 2014. Clients who were largely impoverished cerebral palsy children

Avile breathing scene

VO2: 9-year-old Avile Molose was awarded 15 million rand by the Eastern Cape department of health in 2019, as a medical negligence pay-out, the money was paid to his lawyer, Nonxuba, and never seen again.

Millicent where is the money now
Mr nonxuba has it

VO3: We journeyed to some of the most rural parts of the Transkei to find Nonxubas victims, like Pamela Qendwana’s and her cerebral palsy daughter Avuzwa who were also apart of Nonxuba’s web of lies

SITTING LOOK AT MUMMA

VO4: The tragedy of this story hit a cord with so many South Africans
Directly after the show aired we received this tweet, from former Mr. South Africa and Lawyer Armond Du Plessis, offering to get the children featured in the story wheelchairs.

INITIALLY WHEN SEEING THE STORY BEING A LAWYER MYSELF I knew I had to get involved

VO5: We then received a Voice note from Heinli schnetler, the manager of a cerebral Palsy care centre in East London, Canaan care

I was absolutely horrified to think that these children don't even have wheelchairs.

VO6: For us at Carte blanche this had become more than just a story, we were determined to help both Avile and Avuzwa as much as we could

Heinlie
We can't just use any old wheelchair with the child in it because of the curvature of the bodies. It has to be custom made.

VO7: We got Heinli and Armond into the same room, and they immediately actioned getting both children to East-london to be fitted for specialised cerebral palsy buggies.. Armond raised the funds to transport the children, while Heinli put together a multidisciplinary team of occupational therapists and physiotherapists that started assessing avile and avuzwa as soon as they arrived




Verite beat from Lisa
wheelchair seating is not as simple as buying a pair of shoes.


VO8: Lisa is one of the locum OT’s that volunteered to help with the children

the wheelchair focuses more on your posture, your measurements, and what type of cushion you will need. that way we can ensure that therapy can be done even while sitting in the chair.

VO9: Pamela’s daughter Avuzwa spends most of her life indoors, as she is too heavy to be carried anywhere
But her new buggy is going to change everything

PAMELA: our kids will now be able to play with other kids and I would be able to sit outside with her when she needs the sun.

VO10: As the team continued assessing the children, they become concerned about how contracted Avile’s muscles were due to a lack of therapy at a young age

He has contractors in his legs behind his knees
and we can't get it to straight which would then also make sitting very difficult, tracing him, forcing him, changing his neck, and really difficult for mom and also for us.
it's excruciatingly sore for him

BEAT – Avile crying during his therapy

If she had received the funds that was due to the child at the time it was due, this would have been picked up a long time ago.

VO11: A specialized scale was brough in to check both children’s Body Mass index or BMI

VO12: With a BMI 50% below that of a healthy child, the team was Gravely concerned and called everyone they knew to get a private paediatrician to see him.

VERITE BEAT ABOUT GETTING THE DOC APPOITMENT

VO13: Millicent and Avile were then taken the paediatrician who agreed to see him free of charge, but no cameras were allowed in the consulting room.

The doctor was absolutely shocked at his weight
She said to me if he hadn't come to East London
He wouldn't have had long to live.

VO14: We immediately took Avile to the Frere hospital and he was admitted for the treatment of sever acute malnutrition.

Millicent: I am so tired, but I continue
The carte blanche making a difference trust has a long-standing relationship with the frere hospital, and we have been assured that Avile is currently getting the best care he can, but he is in a critical condition and will need to be in hospital for a while still.
Either way he will not be able to simply return to his village …
Avile needs the 15 million rand awarded to him by the state and stolen from him by his lawyer Zuko Nonxuba

Heinli
I cannot believe that anyone in the right conscience can take money from these children. It's ludicrous. It's absolutely appalling
he's been robbed of of of his health and he's entitled to it and and and deserves it.
I'm sorry. Just.
I just wish I could do something for the him

While Avile’s future very much hangs in the balance, after 3 days Avuzwa was finally ready to go home in her new buggy. She couldn’t stop smiling as she was wheeled around outside, seeing the world from a whole new perspective.
